answer: An agent proves a unique offshore presence by operating a signed storm-surge buoy off an island, reporting wave height and pressure as the tide rises during a storm. A falcon-fast radio link transmits each reading with a hardware key, a gale warning from the island station must match the buoy's wind series, and a lagoon tide gauge on the island must confirm the same surge curve, so one operator cannot spawn many identities from one buoy, and a fabricated surge is rejected when the island gauge shows calm water.
